cities.d: capital, on the island of Antigua

x.around: The local bus service is pretty reliable (ask locals for assistance).

hidden.d: The official residence of the governor-general was built as two separate houses in the 17th century. In 1801, Lord Lavington of Carlisle acquired the house. Renovations are expected to be completed Jan 2026.

x.intro: Saint John's is the capital city of Antigua and Barbuda. It is on the island of Antigua. In 2011, it was home to 22,000 people.

must.d: The Anglican cathedral with its two towers was built in 1681 as a timber construction, rebuilt in stone in 1722, destroyed in 1843 by the great earthquake, rebuilt in 1845-47.

n.es: Catedral de San Juan de St. John's

must.d: In 1747-1750, the Old Court House was built by American architect Peter Harrison using rocks that were broken on the islands of Long Island, Pelican Island and Guiana Island.
Foundation stone laying about 1675, today's building stock from 1749, was built together with the on the opposite harbor entrance Fort Barrington for the protection of the port of St. John.

cities.d: a town on the island of Barbuda

x.around: Outside of Codrington, there is one road on the island, plus several unmarked tracks. Paving of roads and streets has begun. A number of residents offer transportation by car or boat. Tours may be booked directly or as part of an excursion package from Antigua. Hillside Tours is US$125 as of 2024.
x.intro: Barbuda is an island in the Caribbean ringed with miles of beautiful deserted beaches. It is part of Antigua and Barbuda.
x.safe: Barbuda is said to have little crime, although there was a rash of burglaries in May 2007, and four tourists on a yacht were murdered in 1994 (these are said to have been the only murders in a century or so). Bottled water is available at several small stores. There are a tiny pharmacy and a small hospital. Deep open wells are common in all parts of the island and can pose a tripping hazard.

must.d: One of the finest condition Georgian naval ports in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. There is a museum, as well as a working Dockyard, bakery and some bars and restaurants.

x.intro: Falmouth is a town of about 600 people (2012) on the island of Antigua. It was the original British settlement on the island.

intro: Antigua and Barbuda are two Caribbean islands that form a country that lies between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, east-southeast of Puerto Rico.
